findings.statement: CA9 is strongly up in tumour protein (log2FC [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.269]) and replicates in TCGA-KIRC RNA (log2FC [gene=CA9; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=9.712]), with the change surviving purity extrapolation; it is the top-convergence tumour-intrinsic biomarker and has antibody drugs (girentuximab).

Safety caveat: in the GTEx vital-organ proteome CA9 is tissue-enriched (stomach, TS [gene=CA9; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=5.19]), a possible on-target off-tumour concern for CA9-directed therapy.

CD70 is up in tumour protein (log2FC [gene=CD70; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.421]), replicates in TCGA, is tumour-intrinsic by purity, has clinical-stage antibody/ADC programmes, and is not enriched in vital organs (max TS [gene=CD70; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=0.34]), giving a favourable safety profile.

ENPP3 is a membrane enzyme up in tumour protein (log2FC [gene=ENPP3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.544]), RNA, and TCGA; it has an ADC (AGS-16C3F) history and no vital-organ enrichment, though copy-number loss is seen in a minority of tumours.

NNMT is strongly up in protein (log2FC [gene=NNMT; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.709]) and RNA, is tumour-intrinsic, and higher TCGA expression predicts worse survival (log HR per SD [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.301]); it is a metabolic enzyme (not a surface target) with no drugs recorded, best used as a prognostic biomarker.

SCARB1 (HDL receptor) tops the target ranking: protein is up (log2FC [gene=SCARB1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.837]) with RNA and TCGA replication and tumour-intrinsic purity behaviour, but no prognostic signal and no ccRCC drug history.

SLC16A3 (MCT4 lactate exporter) is up in RNA (log2FC [gene=SLC16A3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=3.435]) and protein, replicates in TCGA, and fits the glycolytic HIF programme; grade association is present but survival is not significant.

Negative result: SCD is up in tumours but PRISM shows no ccRCC-selective sensitivity to SCD inhibition (selectivity [gene=SCD; type=prism_response; source=DATASET:PRISM-20Q2; selectivity=0.019], BH q [gene=SCD; type=prism_response; source=DATASET:PRISM-20Q2; padj=0.932]), so tumour overexpression alone does not establish a dependency.

PSAT1 is the top down-regulated biomarker: protein is lower in tumour (log2FC [gene=PSAT1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=-1.963]), with RNA and TCGA agreement and prognostic value, reflecting loss of normal tubule identity rather than a target.

ALDH6A1 is down in tumours and low TCGA expression predicts worse survival (log HR per SD [gene=ALDH6A1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=-0.554]); frequent 14q loss with a positive cis effect indicates a real dosage component, so it is a prognostic tissue-identity biomarker.

PPP1R1A is strongly down in tumour RNA/protein and TCGA, and higher expression predicts worse survival (log HR per SD [gene=PPP1R1A; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.403]); a down-regulated prognostic biomarker with no target tractability.

caveats: Mechanism genes on 3p (VHL, PBRM1, SETD2, BAP1) were not examined in this pass.
No gene shows a selective ccRCC dependency in DepMap or PRISM; target ranking rests on expression, replication, purity and tractability, not on demonstrated vulnerability.
PRISM uses 2D cell lines and misses HIF-2 biology.
GTEx vital-organ proteome lacks kidney and has detection limits; absence of signal is not proof of safety.
Prognostic direction comes from TCGA RNA only; CPTAC protein survival was not tested.
Phosphosite and kinase-activity layers were not explored.
